proposition.claim:
The stated reducible-curve definition makes every pair intertwined, so the nonempty form of Theorem 3.3 used in the main proof is false.

Typicality assertions for every marked critical point are false under the theorem hypotheses and fail for the periodic critical points in the main constructed families.

Infinite PCF parameters proved via P_1=t,P_{n+1}=P_n^2+t: for each prime p, degree 2^{p-1}, simple root 0, a further root gives exact period p. Distinct primes yield distinct parameters. Same family on both sides is allowed.

Critical cycles and zero-multiplier fixed points are counted with different weights.

Degree two; f is hyperbolic PCF of disjoint type (1,2); choose g=f to satisfy the same-spectrum premise if needed.

repair.content:
Require finite projections, or a periodic irreducible component dominating both factors. The finite Corr objects on p.14 meet this stronger condition; a component of an invariant finite union is periodic, permitting the cited irreducible-curve theorem. Original definition must change.

Apply pointwise conditions only to selected active a1,b1, allow a finite initial prefix or use iterated marked sections, and recheck the two-family renormalization with that convention. DAO p.52(b) already restricts to active points; its Definition 4.1 also has the n>=0 issue. No full replacement of the deep argument is certified here. Change b2 to b1 consistently.

u_n=sum_{l|n} l*m_l; m_n=(1/n)sum_{l|n} mu(l)u_{n/l}. A zero-multiplier fixed point is simple as a fixed point, so no additional algebraic multiplicity is needed.
